newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- North Korean defector Hwang Jang-Yop, who sought refuge in the Philippines, has left the country for Seoul where he said he was defecting because he lost all hope in a communist regime unable to feed its hungry people. (ALL PAPERS)
- Congress returns to work with the passage of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package as as one of its priorities.
- Burglars broke into the house of armed forces chief of staff Arnulfo Acedera's father, police say (MANILA TIMES)
- The Philippine Commission on Good Government says it still wants San Miguel Corp to renegotiate for a better deal with Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd of Australia. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- A leading investment bank has urged the country's commercial banks to practice caution in their lending operations to avoid a financial crisis which hit other banks in the region.
- The Department of Finance says the government should curb the rising current account deficit. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Board of Investments is finalising a proposal to impose a tax on a wide range of imported products to help local industries cope with trade liberalisation. (MANILA TIMES)
